relevance_note: Case report of an Iranian family with a LAMP2 variant plus a literature table of all carriers: 'Nine patients were carriers of the c.877C>T variant.'
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I chose. Its Table 1 row-prefix spans were cut from the Markdown rows and checked against the table by eye. Table 1 has no label column, so the seven literature patients are 'Table 1 row 1'..'Table 1 row 7'. Data rows were counted after the header line 'Origin | Gender | ...' and the empty line after it. Rows 8 and 9 are the study family's III-1 and II-5 (paper labels). Row 6 (Iran, ref (9)) is the same person as the Amin et al. (9) case described in 'Previously reported case', so text facts were added to that row. Table 1 '-' cells are not defined as absent in the legend, so they were treated as not reported. Table 1 'Age (Y)' is not defined; the text calls it 'the age range during the study', so I recorded it as age at last evaluation for the literature rows (uncertain). Row 3 (USA, ref (8)) has only origin and reference; the Methods say ref (8) gave no clinical details 'for the two families', so this row may stand for more than one person. 'De novo' in the Variant status column for rows 1 and 4 is not recorded as inheritance, because no parental testing is described (rule 8); parental_testing_statement is left not reported. Relatives named in the Variant status column were given rows: mothers of rows 2 and 5 and two older brothers of row 6 (died of heart failure), and the sister of row 7 (sudden death at 1 year). III-1's father and sister tested negative and are included; they have no features. The cDNA c.877C>T for literature rows comes from 'Nine patients harboured the c.877C>T variant' and the protein from the Table 1 title. Variant type 'nonsense' comes from sentences naming this exact variant. Pathogenicity and ACMG codes ('the candidate variant') are given only for III-1 and II-5. The transcript NM_002294.3 is the reference sequence the authors used for Sanger analysis, and is recorded only for III-1 and II-5. Contradictions and uncertain points: III-1's age is given as 7 in Table 1, '9-year-old' at referral and 'a 13-year-old boy' in the Introduction, with onset at 7 years and death at 14, so age at last evaluation is left not reported. III-1 had 'normal tone, power, reflexes, and gait' on examination, but his family reported later difficulty walking and proximal muscle weakness ('occurred just before the patient’s condition worsened in subsequent years'). I read this as a change over time, emitted both rows, and marked the checklist observed. Row 6 'had no notable musculoskeletal complaints' at presentation but later 'muscle involvement' (Table: Myopathy); I treated this the same way. 'All previously reported patients were male and presented with varying degrees of concentric LVH' conflicts with Table 1 (row 3 sex '-', and only four cases of concentric LVH), so it was not used. Abstract group statements ('All patients ...') were not used. 'The two Iranian patients' (no skeletal-myopathy symptoms at onset) was read as row 6 and III-1, following the paper's own use of the phrase ('differed between the two Iranian patients ... One patient died in their 30s, while the proband passed away at age 14'). EF values (30%, 45%) not described as reduced were kept as features only and not mapped to the checklist. 'Normal mental health and speech' (row 6) and 'clinical laboratory test results within normal ranges' (II-5) were written as the paper states them and exclude no checklist item. II-5 'normal ... muscle strength' was used to exclude the proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy) item. Table 1 column 'Cardiac conduction impairments' = Yes was recorded as a feature for rows 4-7 but not mapped to any specific conduction checklist item. Vital status 'alive' for the four transplanted patients ('four underwent heart transplants and survived') was not assigned, because it would need combining the count with the HTx column.
